messages:
emma: Quick check — we're seeing sporadic 429s during streaming sessions right around when auth tokens rotate. What's the recommended client behavior for streaming vs non-streaming? Should we attach an idempotency key to the initial stream open? cc @raj

raj: Short answer: idempotency keys are great for independent RPCs (non-streaming). For long-lived streams use resume tokens (server-provided) for reconnects. If stream open returns 429, do an exponential backoff + jitter and retry. If it's a token refresh race, refresh and retry once.

olivia: A couple of practical rules we shipped in Node SDK: respect Retry-After header on 429, otherwise use full jitter between 100ms and 5s. Also expose maxRetries (default 4). Keep each retry attempt small for streaming (don't re-send large bodies).

liam: Rust SDK note: streaming semantics differ — server emits a resume token frame. Client should persist that token to disk/memory and include it on reconnect. Don't try to treat resume reconnects as idempotent replays of the whole stream.

raj: Pseudo retry policy we recommend:```
attempt = 0
while attempt < maxRetries:
  resp = send(req)
  if resp.code in 200..299: return resp
  if resp.code == 429:
    if resp.headers["Retry-After"]: sleep(parseRetryAfter())
    else: sleep(random(0, base * 2^attempt))  # full jitter
    attempt += 1
    continue
  if resp.code >= 500 and resp.code < 600:
    attempt += 1
    sleep(random(0, short_base * 2^attempt))
    continue
  break
```

emma: Good. What about distinguishing 429 that are throttling vs 429 caused by an auth token race after refresh? We see both.

olivia: Heuristic: if you get 401 then refresh token and retry immediately. If you then see 429s clustered against the same account right after many clients refreshed, treat as token-thundering — back off with jitter and implement staggered refresh. Also tag requests with a client id so server can detect refresh storms.

liam: For streaming reconnects specifically: on connection loss save last-emitted offset + resume token. On reconnect, call resume endpoint with token. If resume fails with 429, parse Retry-After OR wait with jitter and try up to N times. If resume can't be recovered, fall back to starting a fresh session (and surface to app).

sre-bot: INCIDENT-ALERT: brief 429 spike observed across hosted region-us-west-2 between 2169004120 and 2169004320. Engineers notified.

emma: For the SDK PR I'll: parse Retry-After, add configurable maxRetries (default 4), implement full jitter backoff, persist resume tokens for streaming, and add a one-time refresh-and-retry on 401. Will open draft and ping @raj for review.

raj: Sounds good. Two nitpicks: 1) make maxRetry configurable per route (embeddings vs generation vs stream open) 2) add telemetry counters: retry_count, retry_after_used, resume_success.

emma: Will do. Thanks everyone — I'll push the draft later today. :thumbsup:
